java_locations: sun.font.CCompositeGlyphMapper and CTFontGetGlyphsForCharacters, the own-glyph test PrimaryFaceExtract records as P runs
invariant: A character that a measured face's cmap maps is measured with that face's own advance. A character the face does not map keeps the current fallback chain.
causal_divergence: Verdana, Arial and Helvetica own-closures cover printable ASCII only, so mapped non-ASCII characters fall through to SansSerif. The known gaps are Verdana italic «Ferrous gauge vista» (Java 157.2197), «marker» (Java 61.2366) and Latin+Hebrew m9a_vi_hebrew_italic.
planned_change: Measure mapped non-ASCII on Helvetica, Arial and Verdana from the extracted cmap rows, and leave an unmapped character on the existing fallback chain. The retained 1139-unit guillemet arm is gone; U+00AB and U+00BB are in the Helvetica plain and bold cmap rows. Do not invent an advance for a scalar the face does not map, and do not retarget Times, Courier, Menlo or Lucida.
perturbation_axes: mapped non-ASCII on Verdana, Arial and Helvetica, including guillemets and Hebrew
